# PRACTICE DIRECTION 61 – ADMIRALTY CLAIMS

# This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] Contents of this Practice Direction

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] Title

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.1 – Scope

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] Case management

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.3 – Claims in rem

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.3A – Claims in personam

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.4 – Collision claims

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.5 – Arrest

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.7 – Cautions against arrest

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.8 – Release and cautions against release

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.9 – Judgment in default

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.10 – Sale by the court and priorities

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] 61.11 – Limitation claims

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] Proceeding against or concerning the International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund 1992 and the International Oil Pollution Supplementary Fund

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] References to the Registrar

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61] Undertakings

## 61.1 – Scope

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.1 – Scope] 1.1 Practice Direction 58 also applies to Admiralty claims except where it is inconsistent with Part 61 or this practice direction. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.1 – Scope] 1.2 Practice Direction 57AC (Witness Evidence at Trial) applies to witness statements for use at trials in admiralty claims (including claims in rem, collision claims, and limitation claims) in the Admiralty Court, notwithstanding that such claims are not proceedings under CPR Part 7 or Part 8. It applies to proceedings in the Admiralty Court whenever begun, but only to trial witness statements signed on or after 1 October 2021. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.1 – Scope] (Rule 61.1(2) defines an ‘admiralty claim’ as a claim within the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court as set out in section 20 of the Senior Courts Act 1981.)”

## Case management

## 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (1) whether the claim will remain in the Admiralty Court or be transferred to another court; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (2) if the claim remains in the Admiralty Court –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (a) whether it will be dealt with by –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (i) the Admiralty Judge; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (ii) the Registrar; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.1 After a claim form is issued the Registrar will issue a direction in writing stating –] (b) whether the trial will be in London or elsewhere. ## 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (1) the nature of the issues and the sums in dispute; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (2) the criteria set in rule 26.13 so far as they are applicable. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.3 Where the Registrar directs that the claim will be dealt with by the Admiralty Judge, case management directions will be given and any case management conference or pre-trial review will be heard by the Admiralty Judge. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.4 Where it is directed that a claim is to be dealt with by the Registrar, it is the Registrar who will give directions, conduct any case management conference and any pre-trial review, and try the claim. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.5 Appeals from all decisions and judgments of the Registrar are to the Admiralty Judge, unless otherwise ordered (and subject to article 4(1)(a) of the Access to Justice 1999 (Destination of Appeals) Order 2016, S.I. 2016 No. 917). [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.6 A personal injury or fatal accident claim must be commenced in the Admiralty Court if it is made in rem or if it arises out of a collision; see CPR rules 61.2(1)(a)(i) and (ii). [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.7 Personal injury and fatal accident claims falling within section 20(2)(f) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 made in personam, if commenced in the High Court, may be commenced in the Admiralty Court. Under its tort and contract jurisdiction and its jurisdiction to determine claims for sums recoverable under statute conferred by sections 15 and 16 of the County Courts Act 1984 respectively, such claims may also be commenced in the County Court. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.8 Claims within paragraph 2.7 should not be commenced in the Admiralty Court unless they require or would benefit from the specialist knowledge and experience of that court. That is likely to include personal injury claims—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (a) which involve questions of navigation, seamanship, boat or ship-handling skills and/or acts or omissions relating to sea state;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (b) which arise out of the shipwreck, capsizing or stranding of the ship, or explosion or fire in the ship;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (c) which are employer’s liability claims relating to or concerning equipment or working practices peculiar to a ship;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] (d) which raise difficult or novel questions of private international law or of the interpretation of the Athens Convention. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] Other personal injury claims not raising any such issues should ordinarily be commenced in the County Court or the Central Office of the King’s Bench Division of the High Court. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 2.2 In making these directions the Registrar will have regard to –] 2.9 Where a personal injury or fatal accident claim in personam has been commenced in the Admiralty Court but, at any stage, it appears that it may be more efficiently or proportionately tried in another court, then it may be transferred to that other court on the application of any party or of the court’s own motion (see CPR rule 61.2(3)). The County Court has similar powers under CPR rule 30.3, including the power to transfer to the Admiralty Court. ## 61.3 – Claims in rem

## 3.1 A claim form in rem must be in Form ADM1. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.1 A claim form in rem must be in Form ADM1.] 3.2 The claimant in a claim in rem may be named or may be described, but if not named in the claim form must identify himself by name if requested to do so by any other party. ## 3.3 The defendant must be described in the claim form. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.3 The defendant must be described in the claim form.] 3.4 The acknowledgment of service must be in Form ADM2. The person who acknowledges service must identify himself by name. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.3 The defendant must be described in the claim form.] 3.5 The period for acknowledging service under rule 61.3(4) applies irrespective of whether the claim form contains particulars of claim. ## 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (1) on the property against which the claim is brought by fixing a copy of the claim form –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (a) on the outside of the property in a position which may reasonably be expected to be seen; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (b) where the property is freight, either –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (i) on the cargo in respect of which the freight was earned; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (ii) on the ship on which the cargo was carried;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (2) if the property to be served is in the custody of a person who will not permit access to it, by leaving a copy of the claim form with that person;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (3) where the property has been sold by the Marshal, by filing the claim form at the court;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (4) where there is a notice against arrest, on the person named in the notice as being authorised to accept service;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (5) on any solicitor authorised to accept service;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (6) in accordance with any agreement providing for service of proceedings; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.6 A claim form in rem may be served in the following ways:] (7) in any other manner as the court may direct under rule 6.15 provided that the property against which the claim is brought or part of it is within the jurisdiction of the court. ## 3.7 In claims where the property –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.7 In claims where the property –] (1) is to be arrested; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.7 In claims where the property –] (2) is already under arrest in current proceedings,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.7 In claims where the property –] the Marshal will serve the in rem claim form if the claimant requests the court to do so. ## 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.] 3.9 Where the defendants are described and not named on the claim form (for example as ‘the Owners of the Ship X’), any acknowledgment of service in addition to stating that description must also state the full names of the persons acknowledging service and the nature of their ownership. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.] 3.10 After the acknowledgment of service has been filed, the claim will follow the procedure applicable to a claim proceeding in the Commercial list except that the claimant is allowed 75 days to serve the particulars of claim. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.] 3.11 A defendant who files an acknowledgment of service to an in rem claim does not lose any right he may have to dispute the jurisdiction of the court (see rule 10.1(3)(b) and Part 11). [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3.8 In all other cases in rem claim forms must be served by the claimant.] 3.12 Any person who pays the prescribed fee may, during office hours, search for, inspect and take a copy of any claim form in rem whether or not it has been served. ## 61.3A – Claims in personam

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.3A – Claims in personam] 3A.1 This section applies to Admiralty claims in personam (defined in rule 61.1(2)(bc) as an admiralty claim other than a claim in rem). Subject to the provisions of Part 61 and this practice direction relating to limitation claims and to collision claims, the following provisions apply to such claims. ## 3A.2 All such claims will proceed in accordance with Part 58 (Commercial Court). ## 3A.3 The claim form must be in Form ADM1A and must be served by the claimant. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 3A.3 The claim form must be in Form ADM1A and must be served by the claimant.] 3A.4 The claimant may be named or may be described, but if not named in the claim form must identify themselves by name if requested to do so by any other party. ## 3A.5 The defendant must be named in the claim form. ## 3A.6 Any person who files a defence must identify themselves by name in the defence. ## 61.4 – Collision claims

## 4.1 A collision statement of case must be in form ADM3 . ## 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (1) in Part 1 of the form, answers to the questions set out in that Part; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (2)  in Part 2 of the form–

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (a)full particulars of—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (i) the sequence of material events leading up to the collision;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (ii) all allegations of causative negligence or other fault which the party filing the collision statement of case makes, and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (iii)  any other material facts and matters on which that party relies; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] (b)a statement of the relief or remedy which the party filing the collision statement of case claims. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] 4.3 When he files his collision statement of case each party must give notice to every other party that he has done so. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] 4.4 Within 14 days after the last collision statement of case is filed each party must serve a copy of his collision statement of case on every other party. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.2 A collision statement of case must contain –] 4.5 Before the coming into force of Part 61, a collision statement of case was known as a Preliminary Act and the law relating to Preliminary Acts will continue to apply to collision statements of case. ## 4.5A

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (1)In any collision defence, a party must state –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (a)  which of the allegations in Part 2 of the collision statement of case the party denies;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (b)which such allegations the party is unable to admit or deny, but requires the other party to prove; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (c) which such allegations the party admits. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (2)Where a party denies an allegation in Part 2 of the other party’s collision statement of case–

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (a)  the collision defence must state the reasons for doing so; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (b)if a different version of events from that given by the other party is to be put forward, the collision defence must state that version (which, where appropriate, may be done by reference to the party’s own collision statement of case). [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (3)A party who—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (a)fails to deal with an allegation in Part 2 of another party’s collision statement of case; but

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (b)has set out in a collision defence a case in relation to the issue to which that allegation is relevant, shall be taken to require that allegation to be proved. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] (4)Subject to paragraph (3), a party who fails to deal with an allegation in Part 2 of another party’s collision statement of case shall be taken to admit that allegation. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] 4.5B When a collision defence is filed, the party filing must give notice of that filing to every other party. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5A] 4.5C Within 14 days after the last collision defence is filed each party must serve a copy of their collision defence on every other party. ## 4.5D If a collision reply is filed, the party filing must–

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5D If a collision reply is filed, the party filing must–] (a)give notice of that filing to every other party; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.5D If a collision reply is filed, the party filing must–] (b)serve a copy of the collision reply on every other party (i) within 14 days after the last collision reply is filed, or (ii) where no other collision reply is filed, within 35 days after the last collision defence was filed. ## Case Management

## 4.6 In all collision claims—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.6 In all collision claims—] (1) a case management conference is mandatory;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.6 In all collision claims—] (2) the claimant must apply for a case management conference within 7 days after the last collision defence is filed, failing which any other party may apply for a case management conference;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.6 In all collision claims—] (3) the mandatory case management conference will normally take place on the first available date 6 weeks after the last collision defence is filed. ## Fast track collision claims

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] 4.7 In any collision claim where electronic track data has been disclosed by one or more parties as being in its control in accordance with rule 61.4(4A)—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (1) the court will seek to adopt fast track procedures for the determination of issues of liability as part of its duty actively to manage cases in accordance with the overriding objective, which may include directions—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (a) limiting further disclosure to contemporaneous documents made shortly before and shortly after the collision;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (b) limiting witnesses to those most closely involved with the collision;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (c) excluding or limiting expert evidence;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (d) requiring the parties to provide a memorandum of points of agreement and dispute, to include an agreed plot of each vessel’s track leading up to the collision;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (e) dispensing with oral evidence;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (f) limiting the number of assessors to one, or dispensing with the assistance of assessors;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (g) dispensing with an oral hearing, and instead determining issues of liability only on the basis of—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (i) an agreed bundle of evidence, and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (ii) written submissions, limited to 10 pages or such other length as is approved by the court, on fault, causation and apportionment, in which case the court will identify the date on which the trial will be deemed to start for the purposes of rule 61.4(10)(a);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (h) allocating the case to a deputy High Court Judge sitting in the Admiralty Court, or to the Admiralty Registrar; and/or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (i) making a costs capping order. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Fast track collision claims] (2) The parties should give careful consideration to adopting these and/or other procedures and directions when completing their case management information sheets. The court will give due consideration to any agreement made by the parties which is intended to dispose of the claim in an expeditious and cost-effective manner. ## Shorter and flexible trials of collision cases

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Shorter and flexible trials of collision cases] 4.8 In a collision action to which rule 61.4(4A) and paragraph 4.7 of this practice direction do not apply, the parties will be expected to consider whether the claim is suitable to tried in accordance with Practice Direction 57AB (Shorter and Flexible Trial Schemes). ## 4.9 Practice Direction 57AB applies to collision claims with the following modifications—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.9 Practice Direction 57AB applies to collision claims with the following modifications—] (1) paragraphs 2.09 to 2.34 do not apply and paragraphs 4.1 to 4.6 of this practice direction will apply instead; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 4.9 Practice Direction 57AB applies to collision claims with the following modifications—] (2) at the case management conference, in exercising its powers under PD57AB, the court will consider the options in paragraph 4.7(1)(a) to (i) above. ## 61.5 – Arrest

## 5.1 An application for arrest must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (1) in form ADM4 (which must also contain an undertaking); and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (2) accompanied by a declaration in form ADM5 . [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] 5.2 When it receives an application for arrest that complies with the rules and the practice direction the court will issue an arrest warrant. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] 5.3 The declaration required by rule 61.5(3)(b) must be verified by a statement of truth and must state –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (1) in every claim –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (a) the nature of the claim or counterclaim and that it has not been satisfied and if it arises in connection with a ship, the name of that ship;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (b) the nature of the property to be arrested and, if the property is a ship, the name of the ship and her port of registry; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (c) the amount of the security sought, if any. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (2) in a claim against a ship by virtue of section 21(4) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (a) the name of the person who would be liable on the claim if it were not commenced in rem;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (b) that the person referred to in sub-paragraph (a) was, when the right to bring the claim arose –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (i) the owner or charterer of; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (ii) in possession or in control of,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] the ship in connection with which the claim arose; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (c) that at the time the claim form was issued the person referred to in sub-paragraph (a) was either –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (i) the beneficial owner of all the shares in the ship in respect of which the warrant is required; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (ii) the charterer of it under a charter by demise;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (3) in the cases set out in rules 61.5 (5) and (6) that the relevant notice has been sent or served, as appropriate; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.1 An application for arrest must be –] (4) in the case of a claim in respect of liability incurred under section 153 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995, the facts relied on as establishing that the court is not prevented from considering the claim by reason of section 166(2) of that Act. ## 5.4 The notice required by rule 61.5(5)(a) must be in form ADM6 . ## 5.5 Property is arrested –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.5 Property is arrested –] (1) by service on it of an arrest warrant in form ADM9 in the manner set out at paragraph 3.6(1); or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.5 Property is arrested –] (2) where it is not reasonably practicable to serve the warrant, by service of a notice of the issue of the warrant –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.5 Property is arrested –] (a) in the manner set out in paragraph 3.6(1) on the property; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 5.5 Property is arrested –] (b) by giving notice to those in charge of the property. ## 5.6 When property is arrested the Registrar will issue standard directions in form ADM10. ## 5.7 The Marshal does not insure property under arrest. ## 61.7 – Cautions against arrest

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 61.7 – Cautions against arrest] 6.1 The entry of a caution against arrest is not treated as a submission to the jurisdiction of the court. ## 6.2 The request for a caution against arrest must be in form ADM7 . ## 6.3 On the filing of such a request, a caution against arrest will be entered in the Register. ## 6.4 The Register is open for inspection when the Admiralty and Commercial Registry is open. ## 61.8 – Release and cautions against release

## 7.1 The request for a caution against release must be in form ADM11. ## 7.2 On the filing of such a request, a caution against release will be entered in the Register. ## 7.3 The Register is open for inspection when the Admiralty and Commercial Registry is open. ## 7.4 A request for release under rule 61.8(4)(c) and (d) must be in form ADM12. ## 7.5 A withdrawal of a caution against release must be in form ADM12A. ## 61.9 – Judgment in default

## 8.1 An application notice for judgment in default must be in form ADM13. ## 61.10 – Sale by the court and priorities

## 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (1) the sale of the property under arrest; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (2) the proceeds of sale of property sold by the court

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] will be heard in public and the application notice served on –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (a) all parties to the claim;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (b) all persons who have requested cautions against release with regard to the property or the proceeds of sale; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.1 Any application to the court concerning –] (c) the Marshal. ## 9.2 Unless the court orders otherwise an order for sale will be in form ADM14. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.2 Unless the court orders otherwise an order for sale will be in form ADM14.] 9.3 Unless the Admiralty Judge orders otherwise, an order for sale before judgment may only be made by the Admiralty Judge. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.2 Unless the court orders otherwise an order for sale will be in form ADM14.] 9.4 Unless the Admiralty Judge orders otherwise, a determination of priorities may only be made by the Admiralty Judge. ## 9.5 When –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] (1) proceeds of sale are paid into court by the Marshal; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] (2) such proceeds are in a foreign currency,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] the funds will be placed on one day call interest bearing account unless the court orders otherwise. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] 9.6 Unless made at the same time as an application for sale, or other prior application, an application to place foreign currency on longer term deposit may be made to the Registrar. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] 9.7 Notice of the placement of foreign currency in an interest bearing account must be given to all parties interested in the fund by the party who made the application under paragraph 9.6. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 9.5 When –] 9.8 Any interested party who wishes to object to the mode of investment of foreign currency paid into court may apply to the Registrar for directions. ## 61.11 – Limitation claims

## 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –] (1) in form ADM15; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –] (2) accompanied by a declaration –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –] (a) setting out the facts upon which the claimant relies; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.1 The claim form in a limitation claim must be –] (b) stating the names and addresses (if known) of all persons who, to the knowledge of the claimant, have claims against him in respect of the occurrence to which the limitation claim relates (other than named defendants and interested parties), verified by a statement of truth. ## 10.2 A defence to a limitation claim must be in form ADM16A. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.2 A defence to a limitation claim must be in form ADM16A.] 10.3 A notice admitting the right of the claimant to limit liability in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16. ## 10.4 An acknowledgment of service in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16B. [This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.4 An acknowledgment of service in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16B.] 10.5 An application for a restricted limitation decree must be in form ADM17 and the decree issued by the court on such an application must be in form ADM18. ## 10.6 An application for a general limitation decree must be in form ADM17A.
